title: Granular Audience Phasing Studio — prototype for phased rollouts and audience targeting
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Design and prototype a compact 'Audience Phasing Studio' within the Redwood Console that lets engineers and product managers define phased rollouts tied to audience slices (user attributes, geos, percentage cohorts) and build a timeline of automatic phase migrations. The goal is to reduce operational friction when running multi-dimensional experiments and to make rollback decisions easier by surfacing impact signals at each phase.

Background: Current rollout tools in the Console focus on traffic-splitting and single-dimension canaries. Customers have asked for: (1) a way to target multiple audience attributes simultaneously (e.g., region + app version), (2) an ability to predefine phase transitions on both time and signal triggers, and (3) a compact visual timeline that makes rollforward/rollback operations low-friction for on-call and product teams.

Goals:
- Build an interactive prototype that demonstrates creating a phased rollout composed of 3 phases: internal, staged external (by attribute slices), wide release.
- Allow composable audience selectors (attribute-based rules, percentage buckets, user lists) that can be evaluated in-order.
- Support automatic phase migration triggers: time-based, metric-threshold, and manual gates.
- Show clear rollback affordances: one-click snapback to last-known-good phase, and a compare view showing delta of success metrics between phases.

Non-goals:
- Full integration with backend routing logic or RBAC enforcement (mocked data OK for prototype).
- Advanced experiment statistics engine — we will link to existing metrics and present simple deltas and confidence indicators only.

Acceptance criteria:
- Clickable prototype in Figma with flows for: create phased rollout, add audience rule, configure trigger, preview traffic distribution across phases, commit rollout.
- Visual timeline component with phase cards, indicators for active phase, upcoming triggers, and explicit rollback CTA.
- Developer-facing handoff notes describing interaction states, required API hooks, and a suggested data model for audience selectors.
- Usability feedback from 3 engineers and 2 PMs captured and addressed in a follow-up iteration.

Deliverables:
- Figma prototype link and embed-ready frames.
- Confluence spec with interaction rules, fallback flows, and example JSON schemas for rollout definitions.
- Short demo recording (3–4min) showing common tasks and rollback.

Design trade-offs considered:
- Surface complexity vs. learnability: we opted for a compact timeline with expandable phase cards to keep the main view uncluttered while preserving detail on demand.
- Expressiveness vs. safety: audience rules are presented with clear previews of estimated traffic percentages and a mandatory dry-run preview before committing to reduce accidental mass exposure.
- Metric overload: to avoid decision fatigue, only three primary signals are shown by default (error rate, latency P95, and downstream cost delta), with an option to expand to additional metrics.

comments: 2026-03-02 — Asha Patel: Initial frames complete. Built three phase card variants (internal, staged, global). Added audience rule composer with attribute+percentage blocks. Leaving TODO for metric wiring.

2026-03-04 — Liam Chen: Review notes: solid direction. Request: make rollback CTA persistent and color-coded to avoid accidental clicks; add confirmation modal with preview of metrics that will be rolled back to. Also flagged dependency on ENG-21409 for rollout API support.

2026-03-06 — Maya Ortiz (PM): Suggest adding an 'experimental' label for phases that are running under a test flag; also request quick export of rollout definition as JSON to attach to PRs. Marked as high value for enterprise customers with compliance needs.

2026-03-08 — Asha Patel: Updated prototype to include persistent rollback CTA and confirmation modal. Added 'dry-run' preview which shows estimated user counts by attribute slice. Created Confluence page with example JSON schema and notes for backend mapping.

2026-03-10 — Review session notes: Usability feedback from Eng x3 + PM x2; main friction was creating nested attribute rules. Decision: introduce a simplified 'compound rule' preset and an advanced mode for power users. Action: create two microcopy variants and test in next session.

2026-03-12 — Liam Chen: Submitted handoff to ENG and added follow-up tasks: ENG to implement API endpoints for phase triggers and rollback record-keeping (ENG-21700), Observability to add a signal hook for phase-bound metrics (ENG-21745). Ready for design QA pass.
notes: Prototype emphasizes reversible operations and small blast radius. When rolling forward, system will auto-generate rollback snapshot. UI will show confidence indicators based on sample size rules. Further research recommended around multi-attribute sampling accuracy.
qa_criteria: Prototype must demonstrate commit, dry-run, pause, resume, and rollback flows. All interactions have microcopy explaining consequences. No backend integrations required for the prototype stage.
implementation_handoff: See Confluence spec and gist for example schemas. Key API expectations: POST /rollouts (definition), POST /rollouts/:id/phase-transition (trigger), POST /rollouts/:id/rollback (snapshot target). Engineers should treat audience selectors as an ordered list evaluated top-to-bottom.
risks: Misconfiguration of compound attribute rules could result in unexpected exposure; mitigated by dry-run previews and explicit validation on commit. Metric mismatch risk — surfaced via confidence indicator and 'wait for N samples' gate before auto-migration.
